stemMd: A prize is awarded to any entry that is original and satisfies the technical standard, unless it arrived late. An entry is timely and satisfies the standard, but originality is unknown. Which conclusion is justified?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The stated facts do not establish whether the entry must receive the prize.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The entry must receive the prize.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Every timely entry receives the prize.

explanationMd: A sufficient condition cannot be applied until all its components are known. Nor does incomplete information establish the opposite outcome. The correct result is uncertainty about whether the guarantee applies.

distractorRationale.e: Missing information is not proof of failing originality.
distractorRationale.d: It is expressly part of the sufficient condition.
distractorRationale.b: The originality condition has not been established.
